en.title: First-group verbs and pronominal verbs
en.goal: Conjugate regular -er verbs and pronominal (reflexive) verbs in the present tense.

blocks.title: First-group verbs (-er)
blocks.body: Most French verbs end in -er in the infinitive — this is the so-called "first group", and it is the most regular of all. Just drop the -er and add the endings -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

blocks.title: A small exception: manger
blocks.body: Verbs ending in -ger (like manger) get an extra "e" before -ons, just to keep the soft "g" sound — it is the only change, and it only happens with "nous".

blocks.title: Pronominal verbs
blocks.body: Some verbs always come with a pronoun that "reflects" back to the subject — se réveiller (to wake up), se lever (to get up). The pronoun changes along with the subject: me, te, se, nous, vous, se.
examples: I get up at six o'clock.

review.pt: Alguns verbos vêm sempre acompanhados de um pronome que "reflete" de volta pro sujeito ...
review.en: Some verbs always come with a pronoun that "reflects" back to the subject ...
review.why: In English, "to get up/wake up" are not reflexive, so the idea may feel unfamiliar; kept the explanation as is without adding a comparison. Examples translated naturally ("I get up", not "I raise myself").
